knee_flex.source: 45-degree leg press guides (PureGym, Skelcore, bodybuilding-wizard): press up without locking the knees (15 degrees); lower until the thighs reach roughly 90 degrees or the lower back begins to round off the pad, whichever comes first

hip_flex.source: 45-degree leg press guides: the hips track with the knees through the same range, since the platform moves the legs as a unit; the limit is the same 90-degree depth before the lower back rounds

torso_lean.source: Leg press mistake guides (ISSA, GymPT): keep the hips and lower back flat on the pad; stop lowering at the first hint of the pelvis tucking or the lower back peeling off the pad

muscles.peakSource: Leg press guides (PureGym, ISSA): the deepest controlled position, just before the drive back up, is where the legs work hardest against the load

mistake.name: Lock and round

tells.text: The knees slam to a hard lockout at the top of the press.
The hips curl and the lower back rounds off the pad at the bottom.

mistake.source: Leg press mistake guides (ISSA, GymPT): locking the knees at full extension reduces muscle tension and stresses the joint; going too deep tucks the pelvis and rounds the lower back off the pad, compressing the spine

sources: Contact fact (bar/platform over mid-foot): feet planted flat on the platform, shoulder-width apart, toes slightly outward (PureGym, Skelcore); a real-world description, not a numeric `machine.settings` value this research can cite
